title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π = Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite free group on two generators. It carries the finite symmetries ρ (order 3) and σ_∞ (order 2) of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Π^{~∧} is the corresponding enlarged group. M_{0,3}^{!~} is the set of 'lacet-preserving' automorphisms u of the semidirect product Π ⋊ ⟨ρ, σ_∞⟩, which is essentially the setting of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^.

Invariants. Earlier pages attach to u several invariants:
- f ∈ Π;
- α ∈ Π^{~∧} and β ∈ Π^∧, with u = inn(f^{-1}) ∘ u_{α,β}, where u_{α,β}(ρ) = αρα^{-1} and u_{α,β}(σ_∞) = βσ_∞β^{-1} (formulas 42–42ter);
- ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} and η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1} (formulas 41 and 47).

The relations. Since ρ^3 = 1 and σ_∞^2 = 1, ξ and η automatically satisfy the cocycle (norm) equations (44): ξ·ρ(ξ)·ρ²(ξ) = 1 and η·σ_∞(η) = 1. Compatibility gives the 'commutation relation' (46) = (43): ξ = η·l_1^ν, with μ = 2ν+1 the cyclotomic exponent. So u corresponds to a triple (ξ, η, f), taken modulo the l_0^n, l_1^n ambiguity, subject to these three relations.

Dictionary with Drinfeld/Ihara. Take η = f(x,y) and ξ = f·x^m (with ν = m, μ = λ = 2m+1). Then:
- ησ(η) = 1 is the 2-cycle relation;
- ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1 is the hexagon (3-cycle) relation f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1.
This page praises the presentation for its maximal simplicity: f does not appear; the first two equations are separate equations in ξ alone and η alone; the third couples them trivially, and for μ = 1 it is just ξ = η.

First drawback. There are three equations instead of one, and recovering u seems to require solving the coboundary equations (47) for α and β.

Marginal correction. Grothendieck then notes in the margin that this is unnecessary. Since αρα^{-1} = αρ(α)^{-1}·ρ = ξρ, and similarly βσ_∞β^{-1} = ησ_∞, one gets directly u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(ησ_∞) and u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ). I checked this and it is correct.

Second drawback, flagged as important. When passing to images in (S)L(2,Ẑ)^{±}, the images of ξ and η are weak data. They do not determine α and β in GL(2,Ẑ)^{±}; there is non-trivial ambiguity in solving the coboundary equations in the linear quotient, to be discussed later.

Purpose. Comparing different parametrizations of GT-type automorphisms: (g,h,f), (α_0,β_0,f), (α,β,f) and (ξ,η,f). This prepares the cocycle and composition formulas on the next page, which shows that α, β, ξ, η are invariant under inner automorphisms.
errors: The main text says explicit formulas for u(σ_∞) and u(ρ) need a prior solution of (47). Grothendieck's own marginal note correctly overrides this: u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ) and u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(ησ_∞) follow directly. No mathematical error remains.
Minor: the text writes 'Π_{0,3}^{~∧}' on the α side and 'Π_{0,3}^∧' on the β side, consistent with the previous page's asymmetric (α,β) ∈ Π^{~∧} × Π^∧. Not an error, but it is easy to misread.

ideas.what: Encoding a GT-type automorphism by a triple (ξ, η, f) with ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ) = 1, ησ_∞(η) = 1, ξ = η l_1^ν; these are the 3-cycle (hexagon) and 2-cycle relations, decoupled from f.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon and 2-cycle relations defining GT^ (Drinfeld's presentation), written as Z/3- and Z/2-norm (cocycle) conditions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces the program; these explicit relations are not there

ideas.what: Writing ξ and η as coboundaries ξ = αρ(α)^{-1}, η = βσ_∞(β)^{-1}, i.e. u restricted to the finite subgroups is conjugation by α and β.
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of H^1 of finite cyclic groups acting on profinite free groups (conjugacy of finite subgroups in Π ⋊ G); e.g. f(x,y) = g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y)-type decompositions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; used by Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura

ideas.what: Direct formulas u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ) and u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(ησ_∞).
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ on the generators of the extended free group / on Out of π_1 of M_{0,4} with symmetries

ideas.what: Observation that the images of ξ, η in SL(2,Ẑ)^{±} carry too little information to recover α, β in GL(2,Ẑ)^{±}.
ideas.modern_name: Linear (SL2 / metabelian) quotients of GT^ actions lose information

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags as an important defect that the SL(2,Ẑ)^{±}-images of ξ, η do not determine α, β in GL(2,Ẑ)^{±}, and promises analysis 'plus bas'. This is an explicit study of the ambiguity of GT-cocycle data under the linear quotient, presumably carried out on later pages.
missed.quote: la connaissance (même dans SL(2,Ẑ) lui-même) de ce groupe de ξ, η une donnée assez faible, qui ne permet nullement de retrouver α, β comme éléments de GL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Bears on how much of GT^ is visible through linear and metabelian quotients, a theme in the work of Ihara, Nakamura and others. The exact form of the ambiguity Grothendieck finds might be a small unrecorded detail, but it is probably derivable by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an independent (pre- or para-Drinfeld) formulation of the GT^ defining relations as decoupled Z/3 and Z/2 cocycle conditions linked by ξ = η x^m. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own route, but the mathematics matches the standard Drinfeld/Ihara presentation, and the coboundary manipulations are routine.
transcription_corrections: 'et qu'au moyen d'expressions explicites' is garbled. The sense is that obtaining explicit expressions of u(σ_∞), u(ρ) in terms of ξ, η, f seems to require first solving (47); the exact wording is uncertain.
'Une autre inconvénient' should read 'Un autre inconvénient' (the [!] is inserted above).

The marginal note reads approximately: 'mais si on veut expressions explicites (cf (42 bis)): u(σ_∞) = inn(f^{-1})(ησ_∞) !!  u(ρ) = inn(f^{-1})(ξρ) !!'. The 'inn' should be read as the 'int' of the previous page.
The group written as 'SL(2,Ẑ)^{±1}' has a decorated S in the manuscript; it should not be read as a hatted SL. Hats belong on Ẑ only.
'ce groupe de ξ, η' is probably 'ce couple ξ, η' or 'des images de ξ, η'; a struck-out word precedes 'une donnée'.
